subject: Renewal + Reserved Pool Tier Shift — perf/$ and throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@bluefin.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bluefin.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — reserved GPUs + HW tier question

Hi David,

We’re kicking off our renewal conversation for the Dedicated pool that expires in June. Usage has grown ~2.7x year-over-year and we expect another uptick if we move a portion of real-time scoring to Redwood.

Two asks to start the thread:
1) We’re evaluating a hardware tier move for next term (current A100s). Can you provide high-level perf/$ comparisons for A100 → H100 and A100 → L40S for our typical chat/agent workloads (median prompt ~350 tokens, 95th ~1200 tokens)?
2) If we commit to +40 reserved GPUs, what throughputs / latency targets can Redwood guarantee, and what credits do you provide on missed SLOs?

Happy to set a call — would prefer a short, numbers-first note before legal/procurement gets involved.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Turner
Head of ML Ops, Bluefin Analytics
elaine.turner@bluefin.ai

Attachment: usage_report_q1_2027.csv (summary referenced)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@bluefin.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — reserved GPUs + HW tier question

Elaine — great to hear from you, thanks for the clear asks. Quick plan:
- I’ll put a concise perf/$ summary below and Karthik will follow with an appendix-style breakdown (batching, kv-cache effects, quantization).
- If the numbers look good we’ll propose a 24-month committed tier for the +40 pool (mix of H100 and L40S options) with a throughput SLO and credit schedule for missed targets.

High-level bullets (preview):
- H100 tends to deliver ~1.8–2.2x effective token throughput vs A100 for autoregressive chat when using ff16/awq q4_0 and workload-optimized kernels; L40S is typically ~1.4–1.6x vs A100 for 8-bit optimized execs but costs less per GPU-hour.
- On perf/$ we expect median perf-per-dollar improvement of ~35–55% when moving from A100→H100 depending on batching and prefix cache hit-rate; A100→L40S shows ~15–30% improvement but better price stability.
- For a committed +40 pool we can guarantee sustained throughput (tokens/sec) per-pool and provide credits scaled to fractional shortfalls (ex: 5% credit for 5–10% shortfall, 15% for >15% shortfall).

Karthik — I’ll hand this to you for the deeper numbers and a recommended pricing structure + term options.

Next step: Karthik to share the perf appendix and a draft commitment schedule we can send to procurement.

Cheers,
David
Head of Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Bluefin_MAP_renewal_0427.xlsx (blank MAP template attached)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@bluefin.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — reserved GPUs + HW tier question

Elaine, David — attached is the detailed appendix (h100_l40s_perf_mem_0427.pdf). Key excerpts below so procurement has numbers-first context. I focused on your median 350-token chat loads and 95th 1200-token spikes.

Summary numbers (representative):
- A100 (baseline): 1.0x perf unit, $X.00 effective cost/unit (normalized)
- H100 (fp16 / awq q4_0 opt): 1.95x perf unit, $1.25X cost/unit → net perf/$ improvement ~56% (range 40–65% depending on batch)
- L40S (mixed-int exec): 1.48x perf unit, $0.95X cost/unit → net perf/$ improvement ~24% (tight range when stable quantization pipeline used)

Throughput guarantees (for a reserved pool of +40 GPUs):
- Sustained throughput per-pool (24/7 target): 18–24M tokens/hour (H100) assuming typical request shape and Redwood batching (observed 95th p99 latency < 250ms for single-token generation under configured SLO).
- For L40S pool, expect 12–16M tokens/hour sustained with similar latency SLOs when using optimized quantization.

SLO / credit proposal (draft):
- Guarantee: 99.5% of token generations under committed latency envelope (p95 < 300ms) across the pool, monthly measurement.
- Credits: 5% credit on monthly committed spend if shortfall is 3–7% below guaranteed throughput; 12% credit if shortfall is 7–15%; >15% triggers a remediation runbook + 25% credit until resolved.

Other operational notes:
- Migration path: we recommend a phased swap: convert 50% of the reserved pool to H100 in month 1, monitor perf/regressions with your eval prompt set for 14 days, then upshift the remaining 50% if no quality regressions.
- Cache/batching: prefix caching and workload-aware batching drive most of the perf/$ variance. We'll propose batch-sizing defaults and a KV cache TTL aligned to your latency targets.

Pricing recommendation (term options):
- 12-month extension: standard uplift, H100 list + 8% premium; credits as above.
- 24-month commitment: 10–12% off list H100 pricing; conversion credits for existing A100 credits applied pro-rata.
- One-time swap fee: waived if signed within 30 days of proposal.

See attached for tables, sample throughput curves by prompt length, and a draft commitment schedule you can share with procurement.

Karthik Iyer
Principal, Product — Dedicated 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: h100_l40s_perf_mem_0427.pdf (perf tables and methodology)

From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@bluefin.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bluefin.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — reserved GPUs + HW tier question

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifying Qs before we loop legal/procurement: 
1) Can you confirm the measurement window (monthly) and the exact metric definition you’ll use for "throughput shortfall"? We need that spelled out for contracts.
2) On the 24-month pricing example — can you provide a sample TCO comparison (our current blended A100 spend vs proposed H100 committed spend) with the conversion credits applied? Even a 12-month cashflow table would help.

Procurement has also attached our standard SOW template (see attachment). If we can get the measurement definition + TCO table we’ll route to legal and try to keep the commercial redlines to minimum.

I’ll plan a 30-minute call next week if more context helps.

Best,
Elaine

Attachment: Bluefin_SOW_template_v3.docx

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@bluefin.ai>, Procurement <procurement@bluefin.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — reserved GPUs + HW tier question

Elaine / procurement team — thank you. Attached is a short TCO snapshot (MAP-draft-Bluefin-0429.docx) that applies the proposed conversion credits to your current spend and shows year-over-year cashflow under the 24-month vs 12-month options. 

Measurement definition we propose to put in contract (draft language):
"Throughput shortfall" means the percentage difference between the total number of successfully generated tokens recorded by Redwood's metrics pipeline for the Customer's reserved pool during the monthly measurement window and the minimum tokens-per-month commitment set forth in the contract. Measurements will be taken at the pool level, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and customer-declared outage windows agreed in advance.

Operational next steps: 
- We will: 1) Share a finalized TCO table and the DocuSign-ready commercial exhibits by EOD Monday; 2) Propose a short 30-minute review with procurement and legal on Wed next week to walk through measurement language and credits.
- You: confirm whether you want an H100-first or mixed H100/L40S pool (we recommended H100-first for the chat workload but will provide a blended price).

DocuSign link (draft commercial exhibits): https://docusign.com/link/bluefin-df8247-draft (internal track).

If that timeline works I’ll have Marissa and Karthik stand by for the Wednesday call.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-draft-Bluefin-0429.docx, Bluefin_MAP_renewal_0427.xlsx
